columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: On YouTube, a podcast show is a playlist and episodes are videos in that playlist; creators can convert any playlist into a podcast or create one from YouTube Studio.
YouTube notes that over a billion people tune in monthly, and YouTube is the #1 place in the U.S. to consume podcasts.
Podcast content can appear in YouTube Music with background play and downloads for most shows, often without Music Premium.
Features include podcast badges on Watch and Playlist pages, spotlight on youtube.com/podcasts, improved search/recommendations, and Watch-page links to the full show.

strengths.title: Massive reach and discovery
strengths.detail: YouTube’s search and recommendation systems surface podcast content to new audiences even if they’ve never heard of the show.

strengths.title: Video + audio flexibility
strengths.detail: Formats range from audio-only with a static image to high-production multi-camera video shows.

strengths.title: Central hub for creator brands
strengths.detail: Channels can host full episodes, clips, Shorts, behind-the-scenes, and community posts, formats that cross-promote each other.

strengths.title: Integrated monetization stack
strengths.detail: Multiple YPP revenue streams (ads, memberships, fan funding, Shopping) tied to the same channel and audience.

weaknesses.title: Higher production demands vs audio-only
weaknesses.detail: Video podcasts need more equipment, editing, and time; creators must maintain both audio and video quality.

weaknesses.title: Algorithm dependence
weaknesses.detail: Discovery and success rely heavily on YouTube’s algorithm; changes can affect reach and revenue.

weaknesses.title: Fragmentation with traditional podcast apps
weaknesses.detail: Many listeners still prefer Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and other audio apps, creators often need a hybrid distribution strategy.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. YouTube Podcasts is podcast shows as YouTube playlists/episodes, distributed on YouTube and YouTube Music with Partner Program monetization. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

YouTube Podcasts are video or audio podcast shows hosted on YouTube channels as playlists, distributed across YouTube and YouTube Music, with discovery and monetization powered by YouTube’s search and recommendation systems. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and YouTube Podcasts side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On YouTube Podcasts you can use Audio and Memberships as first-class product jobs. You want a dedicated listening app, playlists, and the catalog people already pay a subscription for.

Using Kahana with YouTube Podcasts

You can use both. YouTube Podcasts keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep listening on YouTube Podcasts, where the catalog and players are strongest. Put episode lists, companion notes, and Club discussion on Kahana so assigned audio is a library item, not only a For You row.
